title: How Death-Proof Cars Work
summary: Josh Clark and Candice Gibson discuss the 2007 film Death Proof and its stuntman Mike's death-proofed Nova, then turn to real-world safety research. A European Commission-backed group, PReVENT, aims to halve auto accidents in Europe by 2020, and Volvo has pledged to build an injury-proof car that relies on digital safety systems rather than the driver. They explain driver panic and reaction delays in collisions, then survey existing features such as blind spot detection, collision prevention, self-tightening seatbelts, and brake assist, and describe future cars that would brake or steer automatically. The episode closes with a plug for the related HowStuffWorks article "Can a car Really be Death Proof?"

segments.title: Opening banter and Death Proof movie
segments.summary: Josh and Candice open the show, shout out a listener, and introduce the episode topic of death-proof cars. Josh describes stuntman Mike's death-proofed 1970 Chevy Nova from the movie Death Proof.

segments.title: PReVENT and Volvo's injury-proof car goal
segments.summary: Candice describes the European Commission-backed PReVENT research group, which aims to reduce auto accidents in Europe by 50 percent by a target year. Volvo has pledged to build an injury-proof car that relies on digital systems rather than the driver.

segments.title: Driver panic and reaction time
segments.summary: The hosts explain the fight-or-flight response that freezes drivers in emergencies. They note that in many rear-end collisions drivers never apply the brakes, and that drivers take about 1.1 seconds before doing anything in an impending collision.

segments.title: Existing and future car safety features
segments.summary: Josh lists current luxury-car safety features including blind spot detection, collision prevention systems, self-tightening seatbelts, and brake pressure assist. He explains that the injury-proof car would combine these to brake and steer automatically, using sensors to be aware of its surroundings.

segments.title: Article plug and sign-off
segments.summary: Josh points listeners to the HowStuffWorks article 'Can a car Really be Death Proof?' and invites feedback at the podcast email address before the sign-off.
